text.p: Accor chairman Jean-Marc Espalioux said on Wednesday that the hotel business was looking better in Europe and he reaffirmed his forecast for a profit rise this year.
He said in an interview with Reuters that the rise of the dollar and sterling against the French franc were "very favourable" for the group.
Conversely, a planned increase in French tax on corporate profits would have only a small impact, he said.

"Based on the figures we had at the end of July, we confirm the results forecast made at the start of June for a rise in pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit of more than 20 percent," Espalioux told Reuters.

"As for net profit, it will show a significant rise, as a function of pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit, of the capital gain from the sale of Compass shares of around one billion francs and provisions set after a detailed review of the assets, notably the hotel assets, begun two months ago."
Accor on Wednesday reported an 8.3 percent rise in turnover for the six months to June 30 to 15 billion francs, with 3.3 percent due to the impact of currency movements.

Turnover from the main hotel business was up 14.3 percent, with 3.6 percent due to favourable currency movements. At a constant structure, the rise was 4.8 percent, with growth accelerating from 3.5 percent in the first quarter to 6.1 percent in the second.
